svg.aria-label: Immutable data: File v1 with content hash Qm123 is shared to Peers A, B and C; to update it, a new File v2 with content hash Qm456 is created. It is easy to verify, safe to cache, free of conflicts and suits content-addressed storage such as IPFS, but updates create new copies, frequently changing data is harder, and versions need linking. Mutable data: Peers A to D each hold a local replica and exchange their edits directly with each other; the replicas merge concurrent updates with a conflict resolution mechanism such as a CRDT. It supports real-time collaboration and frequently changing data, but is more complex, needs conflict resolution, is harder to cache and must merge concurrent updates
svg.text: Immutable vs. mutable data in peer-to-peer systems
Data is never changed. Updates create a new version with a new content hash.
Peers can cache and share it safely.
To update, create a new file
Harder to handle frequently changing data
Need a way to link versions
Data can be updated in place. All peers need a way to keep records consistent across the network.
Replicas merge concurrent updates with a conflict
Each peer edits its own replica, and
the replicas converge on the same state
